name: qr-device-pairing
goal: A phone pairs by scanning the QR code Electron shows and a person approves it on the computer; the QR holds only the short-lived single-use offer, the phone takes no typed connection values, and grants, revocation and the sealed challenge stay as they are

steps.title: Confirm scope, success criteria, constraints, and proof.
steps.evidence: Pairing starts by scanning the QR code Electron shows; approval stays a human act on the computer; the phone has no field for a link, a code or an address. The QR holds only the short-lived single-use offer (version, audience, environment, expiry, host, pairing, code, exact relay origin), read by one rule in TypeScript and Swift; no credential. Spec: specification/features/planned/qr-device-pairing.md. Evidence: work/qr-device-pairing/status.md in the control directory.

steps.title: Implement the smallest complete feature slice.
steps.evidence: remote: pairingOffer codec, DevicePairingService.scanned, offer carries scan text, closePairing and scan in the ports, pairing link removed. Desktop host: offer-owned createPairing, closePairing, status publishes the QR text. Renderer: qrSymbol over pinned qrcode 1.5.4, RemoteOfferCode (QR, countdown, New code, Hide code), phone panel with Scan QR code only, scan notices. Native: RemoteOffer reader, RemoteScan boundary, session-owned scan that Disconnect ends, AVFoundation camera scanner, plugin scan replaces pair, link scheme removed, camera usage text. Test only: SyntheticScanner outside the app target, scan-fixture build of an isolated source copy, fixture computer with explicit approve and deny. Registry: 6 units added, 2 retired; 83 reasons, explain check passes.

steps.title: Add or update focused automated coverage.
steps.evidence: Coverage added: offer codec with 68 vectors shared by TypeScript and Swift; QR symbol read back by an independent decoder (jsqr), including the longest text and a blemished symbol; browser specs decode the QR from a real screenshot; host pairing by scan on a real host (approval prerequisite, deny, renew, withdraw, expiry, revocation); create race; fixture approval at the real relay Worker; scan store, adapter and notices; native offer, scan boundary and scan lifecycle checks; scanner barrier. Guards proven by mutants in throwaway copies (guard/): 4 scanner bypasses, code logged, QR text in status, port without closePairing, extra offer field: each rejected.

steps.title: Run the relevant project verification commands.
Run the new tests against the unchanged product and record how each fails.
steps.evidence: Original product d2456818 with the final test files in an isolated export: remote 3 files fail; Desktop unit 13 of 14 files fail (21 tests, 4 suites cannot load); browser 5 fail and 5 pass with real before-captures (red-final/, before/). Swift checks do not compile without the reader (red/native-*.log). Review blockers reproduced before their fixes: create race 3 of 5 fail (race/create-race-RED.log); a camera answering after Disconnect starts a pairing, 8 checks fail in Debug (scan-lifecycle/native-lifecycle-RED-debug.log). The three adapted existing tests in their original form fail on the final product (red-final/three-existing-tests-ORIGINAL-on-final-product.log).

steps.title: Run the same unchanged tests on the implementation until they pass; record the proof.
steps.evidence: Same test files (red-final/final-test-hashes.txt) on the final source: remote check 135 tests, relay 159, Desktop check 582 unit tests with svelte-check, lint, build, audit and Swift limits, Desktop browser suite 61 on the owned 5813 preview, Hub 426 and 19 (final/*.log). Native on the Mac: Debug 233 and Release 215 checks, 68 offer vectors (green/native-*.log). Simulator builds of the real source, Debug and Release, exit 0 (native/build-*.log). Native acceptance on its own simulator: 78 passed, 0 failed (native/acceptance-run-1.log, native/ios-acceptance/report.json); its scans came from the synthetic scanner of an isolated copy; real-source products scan with their camera only. No physical camera was used. Fresh after-captures inspected; retained captures hold only synthetic, expired offers (retained-captures.json).

steps.title: Close the queued handoff between a scan answer and its pairing; prove a Disconnect waiting behind it wins, on the real session.
steps.evidence: Reviewer finding: looked cleared the look and pair took a second turn of the queue, so a Disconnect waiting between them was overtaken and a pairing began after unpaired. Check ios/Checks/Native/ScanHandoffChecks.swift (sha 73d87542) holds the real session queue with a barrier, delivers a valid scan answer, enqueues Disconnect, releases and drains. Red on the unchanged Swift (scan d002b264, pairing 77177499), Debug: 5 failed (scan-handoff/native-handoff-RED-debug.log). Fix: the look stays under way through the queued handoff and asked ends it and begins the pairing in one turn (scan b51bc2ce, pairing 782e8b3b). Green, same check file: Debug 247, Release 225, 0 failed; vectors 68; limits 46 files; scanners type-check; barrier 4 of 4. Rebuilt on the new bytes: bun run ios:acceptance 78 passed, 0 failed (native/acceptance-run-2.log, native/ios-acceptance-run-2/). Earlier builds and run 1 describe the earlier bytes only.

steps.title: The existing iOS remote adapter unit owns the new native files and declares the scan contract; no runtime byte changes.
steps.evidence: specification/units/desktop.adapter.ios-remote.json: owns.source gains Remote/RemoteOffer.swift, Remote/RemoteScan.swift, Remote/RemoteSessionScan.swift, Scanner/RemoteCameraScanner.swift and Scanner/RemoteScannerViewController.swift (30 files, no other owner); the declared contract replaces pair and a separately entered code with scan, offer, scan-failure and scan-ended; a declared contract dependency on remote.function.pairing-offer is added. units index writes nothing further; units check valid, 1195 units; explain check 84 reasons, one new manifest reason, earlier rows byte-identical; root audit, Desktop audit, Swift limits, self-verify-config and the reports registry tests pass (final-3/). All 38 frozen product hashes still match; no runtime byte changed. Earlier statements that Swift files are not registry units were wrong and are corrected in status.md.
